cohort: 65 patients with central placenta previa and placenta accreta who underwent cesarean delivery.
finding: Abdominal aortic balloon occlusion (AABO) in cesarean deliveries for central placenta previa with placenta accreta significantly reduced intraoperative blood loss and hysterectomy rates compared to common iliac artery balloon occlusion (CIABO) without adverse fetal effects.
mod_finding: AABO was found to be a valuable clinical option for cesarean deliveries in patients with central placenta previa and placenta accreta, reducing intraoperative blood loss and hysterectomy rates.
followup_time: 24 hours postpartum for coagulation function; otherwise immediate postpartum/intraoperative.
